styles.name: Blob Tracking
styles.coreTrick: Every UI element is dressed as machine-vision output (1px boxes with class/confidence tabs, corner ticks, linked centroids) over a dithered footage plate whose boxes are derived from the same figures that were drawn.
styles.colourRecipe: Fixed graphite ground in dark mode (client canvas kept in light); the primary is lifted to 3.2:1 on the plate and used for exactly one locked target; the secondary is only a 12% wash in the plate; a muted that fails 4.6:1 is shaded toward ink.

remainder.what: Footage subject: 13 figures on two paths, shadows, doorway, as a luminance field
remainder.whyCode: hand-modelled scene geometry, not parameterisable by a palette

remainder.what: Detection boxes derived from the subjects (person, group, shadow, zones) and tab de-collision with flip-under / ID-only fallback
remainder.whyCode: layout solver tied to the scene and to the 884px board assumption

remainder.what: Centroid links (k=2 nearest plus long dashed)
remainder.whyCode: geometry derived from detected centroids

remainder.what: Per-box footage processing (revealed groups, inverted persons, primary-tinted lock) and X/Y/A readout
remainder.whyCode: bespoke SVG compositing logic

remainder.what: Deck cover band / closing strip as a crop of the plate via data URI with caching
remainder.whyCode: integration with deck pattern hooks

styles.notes: Core identity is the scene plus the box solver, both code. The board/kit vocabulary (tabs, frames, ticks, counters) is reusable CSS and would transfer to any other tracked-subject art. Light mode keeps the plate dark, so the kit is two-surface.

styles.name: Blueprint
styles.coreTrick: A full engineering drawing sheet (generated extruded initial in four views, with hatching, dimension lines, notes and a revision table) on a fixed Prussian-blue grid, with nothing filled: line weights and 45-degree hatch do all the work.
styles.colourRecipe: The client canvas is ignored (fixed hsl 218/62/24, nudged at most 8 degrees toward a blue brand hue; white paper in light mode); ink is all line work; the primary appears once as the revision cloud, accent as one dimension line, secondary as 6px status markers, each lifted to 3:1 on the field.

remainder.what: Extruded block-letter drawing: boundary-edge merge of the initial glyph, projection to front, section, oblique and detail views, dimension chains and callouts
remainder.whyCode: real geometry generated from a 5x7 glyph bitmap; no palette-level parameter describes it

remainder.what: Patent-sheet light mode: different figure labels, numerals with leaders, no zone marks, no revision table
remainder.whyCode: a second structural variant, not a colour swap

remainder.what: Brand-hue nudge of the Prussian blue limited to a window around hue 218
remainder.whyCode: small hue-window logic with min/max clamps

remainder.what: Do / Don't pair art (line-type set versus filled, rounded, shaded part)
remainder.whyCode: hand-drawn SVG comparison

remainder.what: Project-name and date strings injected into CSS content via tokens
remainder.whyCode: text sanitising with unicode classes

styles.notes: Kit and board chrome is highly regular (lines, hatch, legends) and moves cleanly; the drawing is the hero and is entirely code. Most moves are used by blueprint only, so reuse across styles is low.

styles.name: Clay
styles.coreTrick: Every object carries the same three-layer finish (coloured soft drop shadow, dark inner underside, light inner top) built from a tonal ramp of one pastel-lifted primary, sitting on near-white cards with a primary-tinted shadow.
styles.colourRecipe: Canvas leans 8% toward the secondary; the primary is lifted to a pastel (L>=70, S<=66) for objects with hi/lo steps and darkened shadow colours, while the single capsule CTA keeps the full primary for AA; secondary is chips and one torus, accent only the highlight pill.

remainder.what: Hand-composed art scene: app-icon tile with embossed initial, sphere with a face, torus, capsule, beads, contact shadows
remainder.whyCode: composition and placement are authored per object; only the object finish is reusable

remainder.what: Embossed initial on the tile via text-shadow pair and cqw-based sizing
remainder.whyCode: tuned micro-typography on a single object

remainder.what: Switch thumb overshoot and per-row avatar ramp assignment (nth-child)
remainder.whyCode: positional per-row logic

styles.notes: Highest coverage of the five: almost everything is shadow and gradient layering from one recipe. Style depends on the framework offering a generic "finish" move with param shadows. Tone does not survive a dark canvas without the different --ab-clay-hi/lo values the tokens switch.

styles.name: Corporate Vandalism
styles.coreTrick: A spotless square procurement shell in client colours with exactly one fixed-palette foreign mark per view (Kruger bar over a small headline, label-maker strip, sticker, marker strike), placed in a different technology and at a different angle.
styles.colourRecipe: Canvas pulled to pure white/black; client primary runs the shell (header strips, announcement bar, CTA) and falls back to ink with a primary underline if within 25 degrees of hazard red; secondary is the track and pattern band; muted/primary-text are shaded to 4.5:1 on the form tint; the vandal layer is fixed red, yellow, black, white and a fixed oblique face.

remainder.what: Hijacked notice document and receipt as hero art: memo line, title, redacted lines, warning, signature, receipt rows
remainder.whyCode: authored document layout; composition logic

remainder.what: Pool of four bar phrases chosen by hash of brand + headline so it never changes on re-render
remainder.whyCode: deterministic selection logic over copy slots

remainder.what: Panel and list markup rewrites (header strips, footnote, PO list with struck word, asset tag)
remainder.whyCode: regex edits of framework markup via def.panels

remainder.what: Primary-vs-hazard collision test and shell fallback
remainder.whyCode: hue arithmetic with conditions; the tokens it drives are simple

remainder.what: Rule "exactly one foreign mark per view" and per-slide placement of marks
remainder.whyCode: cross-surface placement policy; selectors differ per board/deck/app

styles.notes: The vandal marks are individually simple CSS, but the style is a composition policy (one mark per view, two layers of colour ownership) which a flat move list does not express. A fixed second typeface also sits uneasily with the typography lock; the style is a candidate for a "restricted use" flag on moves.

styles.name: Cyber HUD
styles.coreTrick: Panels are chamfered by clip-path with a 1px neon edge drawn as a separate clipped layer behind an inset fill (borders ignore clip-path), glow added on the unclipped parent, over a near-black grid field with brackets for target/focus.
styles.colourRecipe: Canvas clamped to 5% lightness with 3.5% primary mixed in; the primary is rebuilt as neon (full saturation, hue-dependent lightness, raised to 8:1); the secondary becomes a second signal or a +105 degree hot shift of neon if it is near the neon hue; accent only blip, lamps and one split word; light mode keeps plain readable primary.

remainder.what: hudNeon(): lightness search with hue-dependent starting points and a blue-to-azure rotation
remainder.whyCode: colour search loop and hue-conditional branches

remainder.what: Second-signal selection (near-hue test, +105 degree shift)
remainder.whyCode: conditional colour logic duplicated in art()

remainder.what: Readout composition on the art: coordinates, lock tag, leader line, callout, segmented bar, gauge
remainder.whyCode: hand-positioned overlays on the sphere art

remainder.what: Product screens: side nav glow and aria-current states
remainder.whyCode: app-only extras beyond the kit moves

styles.notes: The chamfer-plus-edge-layer trick is the one thing that makes this style work and it is a self-contained CSS recipe, so it ports well. The neon derivation is the colour core and is code. Cyber HUD and Blob Tracking share ticks/brackets and mono tab vocabulary.

notes: Schema notes: (1) expressibleAs takes one value but several moves are mixed (e.g. kruger-bar-headline is css-recipe plus a hash pick in the headline hook; contrast-lift-colour is a loop a runtime would ship as a helper). I used the dominant class and recorded the code part in remainder. (2) Kit component moves (button-style, input-field-style, switch-control-style, segmented-control-style, progress-track, named-states) are enum families: each variant is authored CSS, so a generator can only choose among authored variants, not invent new ones. Counting them as moves flatters coverage; I discounted moveCoverage for this. (3) Highlight-word treatments (box, dimension line, pill, chromatic split) are four moves with one use each rather than one parametric move; the idea matches but the CSS shares nothing. (4) `where` for CSS refers to css/aesthetics/<key>.css; the key in usedBy tells the file family. Line ranges refer to the files as read on 2026-11-06. (5) appSafe: false means board/website/deck art only. Kit-family moves, colour moves, caps-mono-labels and corner-radius are app-safe; art, sticker, receipt, hazard ribbon and similar are not. (6) Light mode is a separate structural variant in blob-tracking (plate stays dark) and blueprint (patent sheet); the schema has no field for per-mode variants.
